key_insight: Adding patient-reported outcomes to surrogate endpoints improved machine learning prediction of trial-level overall survival benefit in oncology.
clinical_relevance: Combining patient experience with surrogate efficacy measures may help assess treatment benefit during oncology drug development.
method: Reviewed FDA approval-supporting oncology trials from 2013–2023 reporting survival, surrogate endpoints, and patient-reported outcomes.
Compared models using surrogate endpoints alone versus surrogate endpoints plus patient-reported outcomes.
Evaluated models with repeated five-fold trial-grouped cross-validation and leave-one-trial-out validation.
evidence_signal: Across 100 trials involving 68,987 participants, adding patient-reported outcomes increased AUC-ROC from 0.67 to 0.79; leave-one-trial-out validation confirmed improved discrimination.
watch_item: Validation was limited to the included approval-supporting trials; broader generalizability and use beyond trial-level prediction remain unestablished.
paper_title: Improving Survival Prediction from Surrogate Endpoints Through Integration of Patient-Reported Outcomes Using Machine Learning
